# Phase 3 — Sandboxed UI runtime

**Size: L.** Requires Phase 2. After this phase a third-party plugin can render panes, reference
panels, and settings pages in isolated frames that can reach nothing on the host machine, while
making permission-checked API calls and receiving events through one typed bridge.

## Design summary

One iframe per plugin surface, own origin, zero direct capability. Three layers make it tight:

1. **Own origin.** `app-plugin://<hash>` is a separate privileged scheme served by Electron main
   from the content-addressed cache (Phase 2). Cross-origin iframe ⇒ no parent DOM, no shell
   state, no other panes. Chromium may put it out-of-process (OOPIF) — a bonus, not something we
   rely on.
2. **No bridge in the frame.** The preload/`contextBridge` (`apps/desktop/src/app/main/preload.ts`)
   runs in the top frame only — `nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` stays at its default (off). So
   `window.acorn`, and with it every token-bearing call, does not exist inside the frame. Add an
   assertion test; this default is load-bearing.
3. **CSP served with every frame response:**
   `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'none'`.
   No network at all — a malicious plugin cannot exfiltrate even to its own server. The only door
   is the MessageChannel port.

The renderer-realm module-sharing design (injecting the host's Solid instance for in-realm
loading) is **superseded** by this phase: inside its own frame a plugin bundles whatever
framework it likes. Nothing is shared, so nothing needs to be shared correctly.

## The `app-plugin://` scheme

In `apps/desktop/src/app/main/appScheme.ts` (or a sibling module it composes):

- Register as privileged (standard, secure) **before app ready**, alongside `app://`.
- Host part is the bundle hash: `app-plugin://<sha256>/index.html`, `/client.js`, `/assets/*`.
- `index.html` is **generated by main**, not supplied by the plugin: a minimal document that
  loads `/client.js` as a module and includes the design-token stylesheet link. The plugin never
  controls its own HTML head — CSP and bootstrap stay ours.
- `/client.js` and assets come from the plugin cache by hash. Serving is read-only and
  hash-addressed; there is nothing mutable at this origin.
- Every response carries the CSP header above plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- Navigation policy: the existing window-open/navigation handlers must deny any top-level
  navigation to `app-plugin://` and any window.open from these frames (docs/electron.md covers
  where navigation policy lives).

## Frame contribution kind

`packages/client-core/src/registries/panes.ts` (and `refPanels.ts`, `settings.ts`) gain a second
contribution kind alongside the current component form:

```ts
type PaneContribution =
  | { kind?: 'component'; id: string; …; render: Component<PaneProps> }   // existing, first-party
  | { kind: 'frame'; id: string; …; pluginId: string; surface: string }   // sandboxed
```

Frame surfaces in the manifest carry an optional `formFactor: ["desktop" | "mobile"]`, default
`["desktop"]`. Costless now while the schema is unversioned; it is what lets a future mobile
shell (docs/future/remote.md) skip desktop-shaped panes instead of rendering them unusably in a
phone viewport. Descriptors (Phase 4) need no equivalent — they are form-factor-neutral because
the host renders them.

The shell renders `frame` panes with one generic host component (suggested
`packages/client-core/src/ui/PluginFrame.tsx`):

```tsx
<iframe
  src={`app-plugin://${hash}/index.html?surface=${surface}&node=${nodeId}&task=${taskId ?? ''}`}
  sandbox="allow-scripts"
/>
```

- `sandbox="allow-scripts"` without `allow-same-origin` is defense-in-depth on top of the
  separate origin.
- The frame is instantiated **per node** (and per task where the pane is task-scoped): the query
  string tells the plugin what it is looking at; the bridge pins what it can reach (below).
- Pane ids remain stable persisted layout keys — `frame` panes obey the same rule
  (docs/ui-design.md: panes keep their ids).

Registration source: Phase 2's roster + manifest. A small host-side adapter (in the client plugin
host area, `packages/client-core/src/registries/plugin.ts` neighborhood) walks accepted
manifests' `contributions` and registers `frame` contributions with the plugin's id bound by the
host — plugin code cannot register shell contributions at all; only manifests can.

## The bridge

### Handshake

On frame `load`, the host creates a `MessageChannel`, keeps `port1`, and posts `port2` into the
frame with a versioned hello: `frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ acornBridge: 1 }, '*', [port2])`.
Everything after rides the port — no `window.postMessage` broadcast, no origin-check footguns.
The plugin SDK's `connect()` resolves when the port arrives.

### Protocol

Request/response with correlation ids, plus server-push for events. All payloads
structured-clone-safe. Error envelope mirrors the API's
`{ error: { code, message, retryable } }` so plugin authors handle one shape.

```ts
// renderer → host
{ id: 1, kind: 'api', method: 'GET', path: '/v2/p/board/cards', body?: unknown }
{ id: 2, kind: 'subscribe', channel: 'invalidate:tasks' }
{ id: 3, kind: 'state.get' | 'state.set', key: string, value?: unknown }
{ id: 4, kind: 'ui', op: 'toast' | 'openPane' | 'copy', … }
// host → renderer
{ id: 1, ok: true, status: 200, body: unknown }
{ id: 1, ok: false, error: { code, message, retryable } }
{ kind: 'event', channel: 'invalidate:tasks', payload: … }
```

### Enforcement (the choke point)

One host-side broker per frame, holding `{ pluginId, nodeId, taskId }` bound at frame creation:

- **`api`** — path must match the permission manifest before anything else:
  - `/v2/p/<own pluginId>/…` — always allowed; it is the plugin's own namespace.
  - Core routes — mapped to declared scopes (`core.tasks:read` ⇒ `GET /v2/core/tasks*`, `:write`
    ⇒ mutating verbs). Maintain the scope→route table in one module with exhaustive tests;
    deny-by-default for anything unmapped (all of `/v2/core/security`, `/v2/core/settings`,
    device/backup/audit routes are permanently unmappable).
  - Other plugins' namespaces — denied. Cross-plugin reads happen server-side via capabilities.
  - Allowed requests forward through the existing per-node client (`window.acorn.nodeFetch` via
    `packages/client-core/src/apiClient.ts`) **pinned to the frame's nodeId**. The plugin never
    sees a token, an endpoint, or a Node it wasn't given.
- **`subscribe`** — channel must appear in the manifest's `events` list. The host attaches a
  filtered listener on the existing client event stream
  (`packages/client-core/src/registries/clientEvents.ts`) and forwards matching frames down the
  port. Detach on frame teardown.
- **`state`** — namespaced persisted storage, keyed `(pluginId, key)`, stored via the existing
  persisted-state machinery; quota-capped (suggest 1 MB per plugin). Frame-local
  `localStorage` also works (origin = hash) but rotates with every update — document that
  `state` is the durable option.
- **`ui`** — a closed verb set executed by the host: `toast`, `copy` (clipboard write with the
  standard user-visible affordance), `openPane` (own panes only). No arbitrary verbs.

Rate-limit the port (e.g. 100 in-flight, 1k msgs/10s) so a broken plugin cannot busy-loop the
shell; kill-switch drops the port and shows a "plugin misbehaving" placeholder in the pane.

## Plugin-side SDK

`@acorn/plugin-api/ui` — the only runtime import in a client bundle, bundled into it:

```ts
import { connect } from '@acorn/plugin-api/ui'

const acorn = await connect()                      // resolves after handshake
const tasks = await acorn.api.get('/v2/core/tasks')
const off = acorn.events.on('invalidate:tasks', refetch)
await acorn.state.set('columns', cols)
acorn.ui.toast('3 cards dispatched')
acorn.context                                       // { surface, nodeId, taskId, theme }
```

Typed, promise-based, cancellation via `AbortSignal` mapped to a `cancel` message. Ship it inside
`packages/plugin-api` with its own tests (a fake port pair).

**Scheme-agnostic rule**: neither the SDK nor the bridge protocol may reference
`app-plugin://` — the SDK sees only its port, and the host alone knows how frames are served. On
a future web client (docs/future/remote.md) the identical bridge runs in a sandboxed iframe with
an opaque origin and header-delivered CSP; the scheme is an Electron implementation detail.

## Appearance

Generated `index.html` links a token stylesheet served at `app-plugin://<hash>/tokens.css` —
built by main from the host's current appearance state and **kept in sync**: on theme/style
change, the host posts `{ kind: 'event', channel: 'appearance', payload: { theme, style } }` and
the stylesheet URL is re-fetched (or tokens are pushed as a payload and applied to
`:root` by the SDK — pick one; pushing avoids cache invalidation). Expose both axes
(`data-theme`, `data-style` — see docs/ui-design.md and the appearance token rules). An optional
minimal primitive kit ships in the SDK — plain CSS classes over the tokens, framework-free by
construction — so foreign-framework panes look native enough. Its class vocabulary is **derived
from the `/ui` entrypoint's export list** (phase 0: Button, Input, Select, Textarea, Field,
Badge, Spinner, SectionHeader, Row, Tabs, plus list rows), so first-party Solid components and
third-party CSS classes share one visual vocabulary; a component that isn't pure enough to live
on `/ui` doesn't get a class here either. Live components (the diff stack, Modal, Picker) are
deliberately absent — if the ecosystem wants native-quality diffs in a pane, the answer is a
bridge/descriptor form where the HOST renders from plugin-supplied data, not exporting
components across the boundary.

## Security acceptance checklist

Write these as e2e assertions, not manual checks:

- Frame cannot read `window.parent` DOM (cross-origin throw).
- `window.acorn` is `undefined` in the frame.
- `fetch()`/XHR/WebSocket/`navigator.sendBeacon` to any URL fails (CSP).
- An `api` call outside the manifest returns the deny error and never reaches `nodeFetch`
  (spy at the broker).
- A frame for node A cannot address node B (path is pinned server-side of the bridge, not by
  argument).
- `window.open` and top-level navigation from the frame are blocked.
- Port flood triggers the rate limiter, shell stays responsive.

## Demo plugin

Build a small real plugin (suggest a kanban board or the token-dashboard shape) in a scratch repo
using only the public pieces: manifest, `plugin-api/ui`, its own `/v2/p/<id>` routes from a node
half. It is the fixture for the e2e suite and a candidate exemplar for the future ecosystem work.

## Exit criteria

- Demo pane renders with tokens applied under both theme axes, calls only declared routes,
  receives invalidation events, and passes every item on the security checklist.
- Frame contribution kind lands in panes/refPanels/settings registries without disturbing
  component contributions (layout keys stable).
- SDK published inside `@acorn/plugin-api` with tests; bridge broker unit-tested against the
  scope table exhaustively.
- `pnpm lint`, suites, boundaries test, desktop e2e green.
